events.summary: Neurology Institute rehabilitation cost Rs. 99 million; opening was announced for June 1.
Cabinet directed immediate cancellation of the e-passport procurement process.
Health inspectors inspected 17,761 Vesak dansalas in a nationwide special programme.
IMF Board approved access to about $695 million after completing the fifth and sixth reviews.
Japan signed an agreement for cyclone recovery and freshwater fisheries support in the Eastern Province.
Funding was provided for five mammography machines for public hospitals.
Appointment letters were issued to 515 nursing graduates for public hospitals.
Health officials conducted HPV and ADT vaccinations for Grade 6 and 7 students.
Northern Province Governor and Indian consul general inaugurated Jaffna Vesak zone lighting decorations.
Ceylon Petroleum Corporation decided to raise fuel prices from midnight.
Health Minister issued appointments to 515 graduate nurses for vacancies in government hospitals.
Japan and FAO signed a recovery project for cyclone-affected inland fisheries in the Eastern Province.
Global Partnership for Health and Water pledged technical and financial cooperation for Sri Lanka’s health sector.
IMF board approved the fifth and sixth reviews, enabling a further $695 million release.
Steps were taken to provide priority cards to island patients attending Jaffna Teaching Hospital.
Initial work began toward providing an ambulance boat for Analaitivu.
The President promised special funding for public toilets at needed Northern Province locations by 2027.
Arrangements began to hire a temporary boat service to Neduntivu during passenger boat repairs.
Appointment letters were scheduled for 515 graduate nurses joining government hospitals.
The Health Ministry obtained approval to admit 3,000 additional students to nursing colleges.
Funding allocated to investigate and resolve the Nilwala River saltwater barrier problem.
Funding allocated for crop-loss compensation to farmers affected from 2019 through 2022.
Foundation laid for the first phase of a new two-storey Thoppur hospital building.
Second phase planned to begin next year.
Military agreed to extend daily public access on Palaly Road by one hour.
Ministry ordered nationwide closures of meat outlets, casinos, liquor shops and nightclubs for three days.
Government holiday originally set for May 2 was shifted to May 31.
University opened television and broadcasting studios, an AI lab and a gender justice centre.
Laptops were donated to students at schools affected by recent floods.
University of Vocational Technology officially issued its greening policy.
Mahaweli Authority said it was recovering ancestral lands from private companies for return to the Vedda community.
Four companies were selected and awarded battery storage projects for 16 substations.
Installation began at Galle and Matara substations with Chinese technical assistance.
Initial compensation was handed to 250 selected farmers; remaining eligible farmers are to be paid within 14 days.
IMF board scheduled to consider approval of the fifth and sixth EFF reviews.
Officials said Mannar land issues would be reviewed and presented to security authorities.
Expanded digital platform enables smartphone registration for social security pension schemes.
Health Ministry plans 18 colposcopes for public hospitals at a reported cost of Rs. 114 million.
Twelve new colposcopes have already been installed in hospitals.
Six remaining colposcopes are planned for installation by June.
Police conducted nationwide drug-prevention raids under the National Drug Eradication Campaign.
President directed officials to quickly prepare a plan to protect the eastern coast and promote tourism.
President ordered an urgent study of a permanent solution to recurring Gal Oya floods.
Construction resumed after twelve years at the Nintavur Cultural Centre.
The cultural centre project has an estimated total cost of Rs. 945.04 million.
The 2026 budget provides Rs. 300 million for the cultural centre project.
Basic infrastructure work has begun at the Paranthan Chemical Factory.
Minister said a committee and lasting plan to resolve plantation-area conflicts were planned.
Deputy minister said initial talks on resolving Hill Country residents’ land problems had begun.
Northern Province planned 39,215 hectares of Yala paddy cultivation for 2026.
Kalmunai health authorities are carrying out a thalassemia control and patient-care programme.
Officials decided to expand screening and strengthen thalassemia treatment and patient care.
Construction continues at the new Beligaha courthouse, with completion targeted for early June.
Cabinet approved transferring Galle Fort's former court buildings and land to the Urban Development Authority.
Sri Lankans in Belgium donated funds for rebuilding a cyclone-damaged school in Matale.
Government subsidy offsets the electricity tariff burden for ordinary consumers.
President promised a public-service salary increase from January.
President instructed officials to begin planned road construction this year.
President said funding would be provided for planned water-supply projects.
Construction of the municipal public library building was completed.
The new Batticaloa Municipal Council public library building was opened.
UNDP-funded training for women local representatives covered developing municipal project proposals.
A committee is advancing work to establish provincial chief prosecutor offices.
Trincomalee Municipal Council distributed compost bins to schools and public organizations.
Fisheries officials received nets and compensation for five boats damaged by Cyclone Ditwah.
A monthly daycare allowance was decided for eligible children of Sri Lankan overseas workers; final approval remains pending.
Ten million rupees was allocated for the daycare allowance scheme’s initial implementation.
Applications were called for 50 female inspectors and 2,600 female constables.
Work is underway on a national information system covering children under state care institutions.
Youth bodies planned a national drug-prevention campaign for National Youth Day.
The Transport Ministry signed a contract to import 104 buses for Metro Transit.
The 2025 Eastern Province allocation provided Rs. 14 million for a school building and teachers’ quarters.
The completed school building and teachers’ quarters were handed over for school use.
First phase of town road widening and pedestrian walkway improvements began.
National housing programme began in Colombo North, with construction started for a new home.
Government set aside funding for a digital campaign promoting Sri Lanka tourism abroad.
A multi-year national tourism development programme is planned for launch later this year.
Hospital departments and services are being reorganized and prepared for expansion in a new building.
MP pledged to advance establishment and operation of Sainthamaruthu Urban Council.
Minister pledged to convene an emergency conference on plantation-area violence.
Railway department reported reconstruction work underway on Peradeniya railway bridge.
Three spill gates were opened as reservoir levels rose.
Committee proposed increasing allocations for National Housing Authority housing projects.
IMF board meeting expected to consider approval of the fifth and sixth programme reviews.
Committee decided to appoint energy managers in government institutions and promote renewable energy use.
Funds set aside for phased teacher salary increases.
A newly built classroom block was handed over to Nagamadu Maha Vidyalaya students.
Funding allocated to recruit more than 1,000 teachers this year.
Officials were directed to resolve local land issues and arrange a land mobile service before December.
Officials said they would demarcate the encroached Varapilavu tank area.
Rs. 8.5 billion allocated for compensation to 1,898 employees who left during restructuring.
Government schools in Hatton Zone closed for one day because of heavy rain and landslide risk.
Government plans to gradually remove 100,000 financially stable households from Aswesuma over three years.
Jaffna Municipal Council resolved to obtain legal advice on managing the bus station toilet.
Police conducted national campaign raids, arresting 919 people with drugs.
Officials decided to pay per acre for removing cyclone debris from farmland.
The President ordered repairs to 21 damaged Road Development Authority roads by year-end.
The council plans water and electricity at grounds and cemeteries and memorial platforms at cemeteries.
Construction of a memorial platform at Kaluwanchikudy Fourth Division cemetery began with a foundation ceremony.
Flooding curtailed Puttalam railway services to Chilaw through May 14.
Officials proposed a pension scheme for tea-sector workers with quarterly contributions.
Two Polgolla Reservoir spill gates were opened amid rising Mahaweli River levels.
Minister said electricity tariffs will remain unchanged through September.
Launched first-stage restoration of flood-damaged Alahera dam under Wari Mahima programme
Government agreed in writing to subsidise electricity tariffs by Rs. 15 billion
Yal Devi train service between Colombo Fort and Kankesanthurai resumes
Irrigation authorities opened spill gates at major reservoirs amid heavy rain.
Australia handed over 12 surveillance drones to Sri Lanka Coast Guard.
President directed officials to take steps to start the Ve Oya reservoir project next year.
Government planned a network of public-service digital transformation champions with ADB support.
Irrigation authorities opened spill gates at three reservoirs amid heavy rain.
Police announced temporary traffic controls in Colombo for the Vietnamese president’s official visit.
Sri Lanka announced one year of free tourist visas for citizens of 40 countries.
Repairs continued at five remaining sites on the cyclone-damaged Maradana–Peradeniya railway line.
Sri Lanka and Korea exchanged restructuring agreements covering 18 EDCF loans.
India and Sri Lanka signed agreements for Eastern Province development projects under a multi-sectoral grant.
Janashakthi Foundation began matching President’s Fund medical assistance for children under 18.
Higher education reform review is underway, alongside efforts to fill university lecturer and nonacademic vacancies.
Approval was granted to fill university lecturer vacancies, with recruitment underway.
Cabinet decided to regularise eligible long-term temporary and contract public employees.
Grade 1 reforms are underway; Grade 6 reforms are planned for 2027, with curriculum preparation completed.
Funding allocations were made for the education reforms and preparation of learning modules.
Cabinet approved the national export development plan for 2026–2030.
Russia pledged cooperation on primary healthcare, technology, training and medicine supply.
Sri Lanka and Maldives signed seven cooperation agreements across health, sports, tourism, education and security.
Government approved a Colombo suburban electric rail network, with construction planned to begin in 2027.
Government launched an online seat reservation platform for long-distance buses.
Housing project launched for eight low-income families; each home is valued at one million rupees.
Foundation returned Railway Department land and buildings after a district committee directive.
Police implemented special Colombo traffic arrangements for the Maldives President’s visit.
Seventy registered clubs received sports equipment funded through the Western Province’s 2025 allocation.
Government allocated funds to maintain the fuel subsidy amid rising prices.
Government allocated funds for electricity subsidies covering 96 percent of consumers.
Cabinet approved permanent appointments for eligible temporary public-sector employees.
Vali North council approved a proposal for a tourism welcome arch.
Vali North council approved awareness signs along routes to Valukkaiaru.
Sri Lanka and Maldives announced plans to sign cooperation agreements across several sectors.
Emergency repairs began on two Southern Expressway sections toward Matara.
Funding was allocated for restoration work on Niththakai Kulam.
Niththakai Kulam restoration was 40 percent complete, with completion delayed by Cyclone Ditwah.
